facts.raw_span: A male infant was delivered at 34 weeks’ gestation
by cesarean section for fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
His mother had systemic lupus erythematosus treated with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisolone
and was positive for anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies
The Apgar scores were 9, 9, and 9 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
His heart rate remained between 60 and 100 bpm
physical examination was unremarkable
echocardiography showed a restrictive ventricular septal defect, a wide patent foramen ovale, and a small secundum atrial septal defect with left-to-right shunt
antibody testing confirmed high-titer antinuclear antibodies (>1:1000) and 52-kD anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La positivity
On day 14
he developed progressive respiratory failure requiring supplemental oxygen, bronchodilators, and diuretics
A chest CT on day 36 showed bilateral areas of diffuse ground-glass opacity and air bronchograms
